title: Keeping artistic control at his own risk
summary: Herman has mostly done what he wanted, bearing all the responsibility, and finds it harder than ever to reach the audience he knows exists.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: How about your own case? Now, you try to maintain as much artistic control.
Because you don't really compromise very much, although you look at possibilities, potentials.
Generally, I've done pretty much what I've wanted to do myself. Whether it's successful or not is also my own problem.
And -- but it's been growing more

difficult and more difficult to do it. You really have to assume all the responsibility and then hope that you can get some help somewhere along the line. At least, that's been my experience in recent years.
And it's a very difficult situation, more difficult than it ever was in the past, ever.

Because there's a big audience out there and I know they're there. We're all aware of that. But we have to exploit it the same as you would exploit anything else. And unless you get that help, you can't prove whether you're right or wrong, and this burns me up.
Now, even though there's more people that you would be able to reach, there are now more groups with more kinds of music.
With more media you have to get around to get to that population.
And so everything has kind of escalated. Monstrously.
That's right. But I still feel there's a need for someone every once in a while to try --
To do something to keep some semblance
of what I would hope to be good taste.
